Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations, 247 CMR 8.00, Schedule II support-handling approval proviso

results.Problem: None. Verified independently at the repaired hash e831eac1 against the promulgated text, not against the canonical rule record MA-CII-SUPPORT-HANDLING. Phase-1 blind answer A,C,E MATCHED the canonical key A,C,E. 247 CMR 8.05(3) provides that a certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy technician trainee may not handle any hydrocodone-only extended release medication that is not in an abuse deterrent form, and that pharmacy interns under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist may handle it. Proposition by proposition: A is true because the phrase 'that is not in an abuse deterrent form' is the operative limiting condition on the class of product reached, so abuse deterrent status is exactly what the prohibition turns on. C is true because 8.05(3) names all three support-personnel grades expressly, and Massachusetts licenses each grade under 247 CMR 8.02(1), 8.03 and 8.04(1), so the higher certified credential does not escape the bar. E is true as the direct converse of the same limiting condition. B is correctly false because the bar is confined to hydrocodone-only extended release medication lacking abuse deterrence and does not reach every extended release opioid stocked; I checked 247 CMR 8.02 and 247 CMR 8.04 for any general extended-release-opioid handling restriction on technicians and found none. D is correctly false because the pharmacist-approval-evidenced-by-written-policies mechanism is located in 247 CMR 8.05(2), where it conditions a technician's assistance in transporting and a certified technician's assistance in transporting and handling Schedule II controlled substances generally; that proviso does not appear in and does not qualify 8.05(3), whose only relief runs to supervised pharmacy interns. Actor, trigger, scope, condition and exception are each correctly stated: actor is the three technician grades; trigger is handling; scope is hydrocodone-only extended release; condition is absence of an abuse deterrent form; the exception is the supervised pharmacy intern, which the stem correctly places outside the item by confining it to support personnel. No numeric fact is asserted. The explanation, choice analysis, related fact citing 8.05(1) pharmacist accountability, and mpje_trap are each accurate. Currency: the mass.gov official regulation page shows 247 CMR 8.00 current as of 04/25/2025 and the verbatim section text carries amendment history through Mass Register Issue 1546 effective 1/9/2025, with the operative 8.05(3) sentence unchanged. Method note: the mass.gov PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so the verbatim section text was read from the Cornell LII republication of the same Code of Massachusetts Regulations section and cross-checked against the mass.gov official regulation page for the current version date and against a mass.gov-sourced search extract of the 04/25/2025 text; the official_url recorded above is the official government publisher.

results.Problem: None. Verified independently at the repaired hash 8957348a against the promulgated text, not against the canonical rule record MA-CE-ANNUAL-STRUCTURE. Phase-1 blind answer E MATCHED the canonical key E. 247 CMR 4.03(7) provides that a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours of continuing education in a calendar day. The numeric fact is therefore eight, and the keyed option E states both that figure and the correct rationale. The cap is expressed without any qualification as to delivery format, so it binds the single-day live conference exactly as it would bind home study, which disposes of A and B; the only format-sensitive limit in 247 CMR 4.03 is the separate annual cap in 4.03(4)(b) of no more than 15 contact hours per calendar year acquired through home study and other mediated instruction, which is an annual limit on a different axis and confers no exemption on live programming. C is correctly false on the number: the promulgated figure is eight, not ten. D is correctly false because no provision of 247 CMR 4.03 defers hours earned in December into a later cycle, and 4.03(5) points the other way by providing that contact hours may not be carried over from one calendar year to another, which confirms attribution to the calendar year in which the hours are earned. Actor, trigger, scope, condition and exception are each correctly stated: actor is the registrant; trigger is earning contact hours; scope is a calendar day; the condition is the eight-hour ceiling; and there is no exception in the text, so the item asserts none. The explanation, choice analysis, related fact citing 4.03(5), and mpje_trap are each accurate. Currency: the mass.gov official regulation page shows 247 CMR 4.00 current as of 01/13/2017, which matches the amendment stamp on the verbatim text (Mass Register Issue 1330, effective 1/13/2017); no later amendment to 247 CMR 4.03 was located.
